additions: The inverted null is not a matched control for flaring M dwarfs: cleaning clips upward outliers at +3 sigma (flares) but downward only at -10 sigma (lcsearch.py FLARE_CLIP_SIGMA/DROPOUT_CLIP_SIGMA), and inversion happens before cleaning (pilot.py:83-84). In inverted data real flares become dips that survive clipping and real transits become 'flares' that are clipped; in real data flares are removed. So the 31-vs-32 comparison mixes two different noise populations. Codex's own SEARCH_AUDIT.md:31 and improvements/README.md item 4 flag this. Fix: either clip symmetrically for both polarities, or run the null with the same asymmetric clip applied before inversion, and report both.

Pre-registration timing failure that the brief under-weights: the tweet (11 Oct 11:12 UTC) preceded the validation pack (21:04 IST) by ~4.5 h; at tweet time no FPP, no centroid/dilution test and no Kepler-169 timing test existed. Public language should be gated on the FPP/NFPP numbers, not on the first-screen pass.

Regression to the mean is visible and should be expected: discovery-subset depth 2,268 +/- 120 ppm vs held-out 1,929 +/- 159 ppm (raw-PSF vet), 1,959 vs 1,563 ppm (event_stats). A signal selected as the maximum of a BLS search over a discovery set is biased high; the holdout depth is the unbiased estimate and should be the headline depth in any write-up.

The pipeline's second peak for the candidate (24.678 d, BLS SNR 8.1, holdout SNR -1.2, max_ses_frac 0.73) is a textbook noise peak and a useful calibration example of what a failing signal looks like in the same star; keep such rank-2 outputs in evidence packs.

The ranked pool is faint: of the 1,800 selected sources, rank 1 is G 14.19, rank 64 is G 16.88, rank 576 is G 18.21, rank 1,800 is G 19.00 (reproduced here). Kepler Bonus quotes CDPP < 100 ppm only for G < 16 (arXiv:2310.17733 abstract); the candidate at G 16.28 already has ~1,000 ppm per-30-min scatter (prep_kepler OOT rms 1,095 ppm). So ranks 577-1800 were mostly stars where a ~2,000 ppm, 2-h event is marginal per transit, and 'no second candidate' is weak evidence about the pool. For a new search, consider a brighter/less-crowded subset of the 406,548 background sources instead of the M-star list, and inject-recover before interpreting null outcomes.

Known-object test should list all KOIs/TCEs within the chosen radius: within +/-5 arcmin there are also K03784.01 (KIC 5688997, FP, 23.87 d, 6,386 ppm) and Kepler-1369 b (25.87 d), plus a 199.59 d Kepler-169 TCE (live TAP box queries). Also search Kepler EB catalogue and Gaia DR3 vari_eclipsing_binary (Codex did, via build_background_prior.py).

Proper-motion propagation (recipe step 14) is immaterial for this star: Gaia pmra -5.40, pmdec +2.85 mas/yr -> ~0.03 arcsec between Gaia epoch 2016.0 and Kepler 2009-2013, versus 3.98 arcsec pixels. Keep it in the general recipe for high-PM nearby stars, but do not list it as a flaw of Kuber's localisation.

Sanity check of the 'M dwarf' label (not done explicitly in the repo): Gaia G 16.282, parallax 3.4065 mas -> M_G = 8.94, BP-RP 2.194, consistent with an early-M dwarf (Barber et al. 2022 Table 5 gives M1.6; TIC Teff 3633 K, R 0.507 Rsun). The 7.1 arcsec neighbour has parallax 0.30 +/- 0.23 mas, so it is a distant unrelated star.

Kepler systematics check missing from the repo: event epochs were never compared with momentum-dump/quality-flag cadences or with the Kepler rolling-band/thermal systematics (only SAP_QUALITY == 0 filtering, pilot.py:60). A reviewer would ask for the distribution of in-transit cadences versus quality bits and versus quarter boundaries (Kepler Data Characteristics Handbook). Label: recommended addition, no evidence that it would change the result.

TRICERATOPS 1.1.0 behaviour change: calc_probs now defaults to dilution_corrected=True (input assumed deblended, as PSF flux is); pass dilution_corrected=False for raw SAP apertures. It also accepts a list of contrast curves, a molusc_file, exptime in days and nsamples; Kepler/K2 are supported via mission='Kepler'/'K2'. Because it pins pytransit==2.2 (NumPy-1-era), install it in its own venv (Python 3.13 is supported via numpy>=2.1 shims). MOLUSC is GitHub-only (not on PyPI).

RNAAS format facts: 1,500 words total including the 150-word abstract, title, captions and references; one figure OR one table; moderated by an editor, not peer reviewed; typically online within days of acceptance. Kuber's 1,196-word/one-figure note complied, so the decline was on substance (unvalidated candidate, FPP 0.069, unresolved prior-search status, TESS non-recovery).
